new.title: Walk the ramparts of the Vauban Citadel
new.desc: The Citadelle de Besançon is a 17th-century fortress designed by Vauban, begun in 1668 and finished in 1711. It has been on the UNESCO list since 2008 as part of the Fortifications of Vauban and houses three museums.
new.tip: Allow half a day and check opening times on citadelle.com. The climb from the town centre is steep, so wear good shoes.
new.q: Citadelle de Besançon, Rue des Fusillés de la Résistance, Besançon

new.title: See the astronomical clock in Saint-Jean cathedral
new.desc: Auguste-Lucien Vérité built the clock in the cathedral bell tower between 1858 and 1860. It has more than 30,000 parts and 57 dials showing planets, eclipses and tide times in various ports, and it has been a listed monument since 1991.
new.tip: The clock is reached on its own timetable and has been stopped pending restoration, so ask at the tourist office about the mediation visit first.
new.q: Cathédrale Saint-Jean, Rue de la Convention, Besançon

new.title: Explore watchmaking at the Musée du Temps
new.desc: The museum fills the Palais Granvelle, a Renaissance palace built between 1533 and 1542 at 96 Grande Rue. It traces the history of timekeeping and Besançon's watchmaking tradition, with a Foucault pendulum in the tower.
new.tip: Finish at the rooftop panorama over the old town. Closed on some Mondays, so check hours first.
new.q: Musée du Temps, Palais Granvelle, 96 Grande Rue, Besançon

new.title: Visit France's oldest public museum, the MBAA
new.desc: The Musée des Beaux-Arts et d'Archéologie at 1 place de la Révolution grew out of a collection opened to the public in the late 17th century. It reopened in November 2018 after four years of renovation, with a refit led by architect Adelfo Scaranello.
new.tip: The collection includes a Bronzino Lamentation. Plan two hours.
new.q: Musée des Beaux-Arts et d'Archéologie, 1 Place de la Révolution, Besançon

new.title: Step into Victor Hugo's birthplace on Grande Rue
new.desc: Victor Hugo was born in this house at 140 Grande Rue on Place Victor Hugo, a listed monument since 1942. It became a museum in 2013 devoted to his life, writing and fights for freedom and social justice.
new.tip: Opening hours change by season, so check ahead. The square also has Courbet and Lumière brothers connections.
new.q: Maison natale de Victor Hugo, 140 Grande Rue, Besançon

new.title: Admire the Roman Porte Noire arch
new.desc: The Porte Noire is a Gallo-Roman triumphal arch from about 175 AD, 16.56 m high and built of Vergenne stone. It stood at the south end of the Roman cardo, became a city gate in late antiquity and was restored in 2011.
new.tip: Free to see, right beside the cathedral, so combine the two.
new.q: Porte Noire, Rue de la Convention, Besançon

new.title: Look across to the Citadel from Fort Griffon
new.desc: Vauban rebuilt Fort Griffon from 1680 on the right bank of the Doubs, facing the Citadel. It was listed as a historic monument in 1942 and joined the UNESCO Vauban fortifications in 2008.
new.tip: Reached by steep lanes from the Battant quarter. It is mainly a viewpoint and a stop on the fortification walks.
new.q: Fort Griffon, Chemin de Fort Griffon, Besançon

new.title: Visit the Resistance and Deportation Museum
new.desc: The museum inside the Citadel opened in 1971 on the initiative of former deportee Denise Lorach. After a 16-month renovation it reopened on 8 September 2023 and is known for its collection of concentration-camp art.
new.tip: Included in the Citadel ticket. Allow at least an hour.
new.q: Musée de la Résistance et de la Déportation, Citadelle, 99 Rue des Fusillés de la Résistance, Besançon

new.title: Shop for Morteau sausage and cancoillotte at the Halles
new.desc: The covered market at 2 rue Claude Goudimel hosts a stall selling Morteau sausage from Simon Saveurs, which took over the butcher stand in June 2025. A cheesemaker stall sells homemade cancoillotte beside Comté and Morbier.
new.tip: Hours differ between sources: plan for a morning visit from Tuesday to Saturday and confirm with the city.
new.q: Halles Beaux-Arts, 2 Rue Claude Goudimel, Besançon

new.title: Order Morteau sausage at Bistrot La Charrette
new.desc: A Toque-rated bistro near the Marché Beaux-Arts, its menu leans on Franche-Comté produce. Dishes include scallops with Morteau sausage and sauces made with cancoillotte and vin jaune.
new.tip: Book for dinner. Ask what is on the daily slate.
new.q: Bistrot La Charrette, Besançon

new.title: Try a Vesoncio burger at L'Oiseau du Temps
new.desc: A bistro in the Conservatoire building, its menu includes a burger built on Morteau sausage steak and a scallop gratin with cancoillotte.
new.tip: Good for lunch before the Grande Rue museums. Check opening days.
new.q: Loiseau du Temps, Place de la Révolution, Besançon

new.title: Taste oak-aged beer at Brasserie du Levain
new.desc: A micro-brewery and bar on Grande Rue near Place Victor Hugo that brews spontaneously fermented beers. They ferment and age in oak barrels in cellars under the city centre.
new.tip: Pair a beer with a cheese board. Open evenings, so check days.
new.q: Brasserie Levain, 138 Grande Rue, Besançon

new.title: Sip regional craft beer at Bières & Caetera
new.desc: A bar-cave on rue des Granges specialised in local and regional craft beers, with bottles, draught pints and one-litre growlers. The shop also organises the Bières en boucle festival at the Citadel.
new.tip: Take a growler to go or taste on site. Check evening hours.
new.q: Bières & Caetera, Rue des Granges, Besançon

new.title: Cruise the Boucle du Doubs on Le Battant
new.desc: The Vedettes de Besançon run a commented 1h15 cruise around the Doubs loop that encircles the old town and its fortifications. It passes locks and the tunnel under the Citadel.
new.tip: Boarding is at Pont de la République on the tram side, daily April to October. Confirm fares on vedettesdebesancon.com.
new.q: Vedettes de Besançon, Pont de la République, Besançon

new.title: Stroll Promenade Micaud and ride EuroVelo 6
new.desc: Laid out in 1840, the 3-hectare Promenade Micaud follows the Doubs with views of the ramparts and Citadel. The EuroVelo 6 greenway passes through Besançon, and a 30 km riverside loop starts at the tourist office by the park.
new.tip: Free and flat. Bike hire is available in town.
new.q: Promenade Micaud, Besançon

new.title: Hike to Fort de Chaudanne for the old town panorama
new.desc: The fort sits on Chaudanne hill at about 422 m and overlooks the Citadel and the historic centre. A circuit of roughly 5.6 km with a moderate climb reaches it.
new.tip: Access to the fort itself may be limited by renovation, but the viewpoint trail is free. Check current status.
new.q: Fort de Chaudanne, Besançon

new.title: Tour Ledoux's Royal Saltworks at Arc-et-Senans
new.desc: Claude-Nicolas Ledoux built the Saline Royale between 1775 and 1779 as an ideal industrial town, listed by UNESCO in 1982. It closed in 1895 and now includes the Ledoux museum, the only one in Europe devoted to an architect.
new.tip: Open daily with longer hours April to October. A combined ticket exists with the Grande Saline in Salins.
new.q: Saline royale d'Arc-et-Senans, 25610 Arc-et-Senans

new.title: See Courbet's world at the Musée Courbet in Ornans
new.desc: The museum spans three adjoining buildings including the Hôtel Hébert, where Courbet lived as a boy, and has 16 exhibition rooms. The Hôtel Hébert has been a listed monument since 1982.
new.tip: Combine with a stroll along the Loue and the house fronts Courbet painted.
new.q: Musée Courbet, 1 Place Robert Fernier, Ornans

new.title: Visit Château de Joux, Toussaint Louverture's prison
new.desc: The fortress at La Cluse-et-Mijoux is where Toussaint Louverture was imprisoned and died on 7 April 1803. A themed tour follows his last months.
new.tip: Usually open from April to mid-November. The guided tour is not suited to strollers or people with vertigo.
new.q: Château de Joux, Route du Château, La Cluse-et-Mijoux

new.title: Browse the Musée de l'Aventure Peugeot in Sochaux
new.desc: The museum occupies a former industrial building on the Sochaux site and was created by the association L'Aventure Peugeot, formed in 1982. Its collection covers Peugeot history from the early 19th century, including the 1891 Vis-à-vis.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 18:00 per the 2024 timetable. There is a restaurant overlooking the collection.
new.q: Musée de l'Aventure Peugeot, Carrefour de l'Europe, Sochaux

new.title: Find the Source de la Loue at Ouhans
new.desc: The Loue springs from a cliff cave near Ouhans, one of the Doubs' great karst resurgences. A path of about 4.9 km round trip leads to it and on to the Grand Saut viewpoint.
new.tip: Parking is 400 m before the source. A municipal order has closed part of the path for rockfall in the past, so check at the tourist office.
new.q: Source de la Loue, Ouhans

new.title: Wander to the Source du Lison and Grotte Sarrazine
new.desc: The Lison rises in a gorge at Nans-sous-Sainte-Anne. A 6 km loop passes the Creux Billard and the Grotte Sarrazine, the overflow of the underground Lison system.
new.tip: Free, with a car park about 100 m from the spring. The grotte is best seen after long rain.
new.q: Source du Lison, Nans-sous-Sainte-Anne

new.title: Explore Baume-les-Messieurs abbey and its caves
new.desc: The village sits inside a dead-end reculée valley around a former Benedictine abbey. The caves have about 500 m of developed galleries with five large chambers, visited from April to September.
new.tip: Combined tickets exist for the abbey and caves. A tufa waterfall closes the valley.
new.q: Abbaye de Baume-les-Messieurs, Baume-les-Messieurs

new.title: Gaze over the vineyards from Château-Chalon
new.desc: This Plus Beaux Village de France is perched on a cliff above the vines of the Château-Chalon appellation, recognised in 1936 and made only from Savagnin as vin jaune. The village has four viewpoints over the vineyard.
new.tip: Half a day is enough. Pair it with Baume-les-Messieurs nearby.
new.q: Château-Chalon, 39210 Château-Chalon

new.title: Visit Louis Pasteur's house and laboratory in Arbois
new.desc: The Maison de Louis Pasteur at 83 rue de Courcelles is preserved intact, from the billiard table to the personal laboratory. It was labelled a Maison des Illustres in 2013.
new.tip: Reserve by phone on 03 84 66 11 72. Hours vary by season.
new.q: Maison de Louis Pasteur, 83 Rue de Courcelles, Arbois

new.title: Descend into the Grande Saline of Salins-les-Bains
new.desc: Salins' saltworks have a 165 m underground gallery with 13th-century vaults, reached by about fifty steps at around 12 degrees. The guided tour lasts about 1h30 and is followed by free access to the salt museum.
new.tip: The gallery is guided only, with departures every 30 minutes in busy periods. A combined ticket with Arc-et-Senans costs 23.50 euros.
new.q: Grande Saline, 3 Place des Salines, Salins-les-Bains

new.title: Learn about pipes and diamonds in Saint-Claude
new.desc: The Musée de la Pipe et du Diamant at 1 place Jacques Faizant shows the two crafts that made Saint-Claude famous. The nearby cathedral of Saint-Pierre, Saint-Paul and Saint-André was built from the 14th to the 18th century.
new.tip: Pair it with the cathedral. Check current hours.
new.q: Musée de la Pipe et du Diamant, 1 Place Jacques Faizant, Saint-Claude

new.title: Wander the Canal des Tanneurs in old Dole
new.desc: The tanners' canal at the foot of the old town gives Dole its nickname of Little Venice of the Jura. The Gothic-Renaissance collegiate church of Notre-Dame rises above it with a 73 m bell tower, and Pasteur's birthplace at 43 rue Pasteur stands nearby.
new.tip: Climb from the canal up the cobbled lanes to the collegiate church. Allow one to two hours.
new.q: Canal des Tanneurs, Dole

new.title: Visit Le Corbusier's chapel at Ronchamp
new.desc: Notre-Dame du Haut is Le Corbusier's hilltop chapel at 13 rue de la Chapelle, UNESCO-listed in 2016. The wider hill also has buildings by Jean Prouvé and Renzo Piano.
new.tip: Open year-round after its 2025 restoration, with paid entry. Plan one to one and a half hours.
new.q: Chapelle Notre-Dame du Haut, 13 Rue de la Chapelle, Ronchamp

new.title: See Gérôme's paintings at Vesoul's Musée Georges-Garret
new.desc: The museum occupies a former Ursuline convent at 1 rue des Ursulines. It holds about a dozen canvases by Jean-Léon Gérôme and his pupils.
new.tip: One listing gives Wednesday and Friday to Sunday afternoons, so check before going. Climb La Motte hill afterwards for the panorama.
new.q: Musée Georges-Garret, 1 Rue des Ursulines, Vesoul

new.title: Visit Gray's Musée Baron Martin and its Saône quays
new.desc: The museum occupies the former château fort of Gray and holds works from the 15th century to today. Below it the Saône flows past quays and the old stone bridge, historically a border of the Holy Roman Empire.
new.tip: The Carmelite chapel hosts summer exhibitions. Walk the quays after the museum.
new.q: Musée Baron Martin, Rue du Tertre du Château, Gray

new.title: Explore Pesmes, a medieval village above the Ognon
new.desc: Pesmes holds the Plus Beaux Villages de France and Cité de Caractère labels. Its château stands on a rocky spur with a 40 m drop to the Ognon, and the village became French in 1678.
new.tip: Walk to the Saint-Hilaire church and the old forges. A guided visit is run by the tourist office.
new.q: Château de Pesmes, Pesmes

new.title: Walk the park of Château de Ray-sur-Saône
new.desc: The château and its terraced park are listed as historic monuments, with a garden of about six hectares. Regional sources describe it variously as French-style terraces and an English-style park.
new.tip: The château is visited only on guided tours. The park is free from Easter to All Saints.
new.q: Château de Ray-sur-Saône, Ray-sur-Saône

new.title: Admire Luxeuil's basilica and the Maison du Cardinal Jouffroy
new.desc: The basilica of Saint-Pierre and Saint-Paul was built from 1230 to 1330 as an abbey church and became a minor basilica in 1926. Its 1617 organ is among the oldest in Franche-Comté, and the Cardinal Jouffroy house has one of the oldest suspended stone balconies in France.
new.tip: The Jouffroy house is at 53 rue Victor Genoux, a few minutes' walk from the basilica.
new.q: Basilique Saint-Pierre et Saint-Paul, Place Saint-Pierre, Luxeuil-les-Bains

new.title: Tour the Maison de la Vache qui rit in Lons-le-Saunier
new.desc: Created in 2009 at 25 rue Richebourg, it presents one of France's biggest 20th-century industrial and marketing stories. The visit ends in the shop with a tasting of products from the Bel group.
new.tip: Use the tablet or audioguide. Opening outside school holidays is limited, so check the site.
new.q: La Maison de la Vache qui rit, 25 Rue Richebourg, Lons-le-Saunier

new.title: Hike the Cascades du Hérisson
new.desc: The main path is about 7.4 km round trip along the Hérisson and passes seven major falls, including L'Éventail at 65 m and Le Grand Saut at 60 m. Expect about 300 m of climb and roughly three hours.
new.tip: Parking at Ménétrux is paid; Bonlieu and Ilay are free. Paths are slippery and busy in summer, so spring or autumn is best.
new.q: Maison des Cascades, Menétrux-en-Joux

new.title: Take the boat to the Saut du Doubs falls
new.desc: The 27 m fall lies on the French-Swiss border between Villers-le-Lac and Les Brenets. Boats leave from Villers-le-Lac, including an electric-solar commented cruise with a stop at the foot of the falls.
new.tip: Boats run in season. You can also walk to the belvedères from Villers-le-Lac.
new.q: Bateaux du Saut du Doubs, Villers-le-Lac

new.title: Walk the tour of Lac de Saint-Point from Malbuisson
new.desc: The official circuit n°24 starts at the Maison du Temps Libre in Malbuisson and loops through Montperreux, Oye-et-Pallet and Saint-Point-Lac. The full walk is around 20 to 23 km, and the Source Bleue lies on the way.
new.tip: Rated easy by the tourist office. An electric-solar boat also sails from Malbuisson.
new.q: Maison du Temps Libre, Malbuisson

new.title: Browse the Lumières de Noël market in Montbéliard
new.desc: The Christmas market and lights run across the town centre, with about 170 chalets around the Saint-Martin temple, square Sponeck and place Velotte. The château of the Dukes of Württemberg is among the illuminated monuments.
new.tip: The 2026 listing gives 21 November to 24 December. Confirm dates on lumieres-de-noel.fr.
new.q: Place Saint-Martin, Montbéliard

new.title: Ride the Morond chairlift for the Alpine panorama
new.desc: The six-seat Morond chairlift in Métabief is open to pedestrians. From the top it is about a 15-minute walk to the Mont d'Or summit, with views of the Alps and Mont Blanc on clear days.
new.tip: Pick a clear day. Check summer opening of the lift with the resort.
new.q: Télésiège du Morond, Métabief

new.title: Hike the Gorges du Doubs from Goumois
new.desc: A loop from the Biaufond bridge climbs through the gorges past the Échelles de la Mort to the Vieilles Femelles viewpoint. A shorter 12.5 km circuit from Goumois tells the valley's mill history.
new.tip: The mountain path is exposed and difficult in places, so wear sturdy shoes and check trail conditions.
new.q: Goumois, Doubs

new.title: Taste aged Comté in the Fort des Rousses cellars
new.desc: The former fortress at about 1,150 m hosts one of Europe's largest Comté ageing cellars, with more than 100,000 wheels of Juraflore Comté. The guided visit lasts about 1h30 and ends with a tasting of several ages.
new.tip: Book ahead as places are limited, and bring warm clothes for the 8 degree cellars. No photos inside.
new.q: Fort des Rousses, Les Rousses

new.title: Walk the shore of Lac des Rousses
new.desc: An easy lakeside walk of about 1h30 follows the Grande Traversée du Jura toward Bois d'Amont. It looks over the lake, the Dent de Vaulion and the Noirmont, and returns through a peatland golf area.
new.tip: Free and flat. For a long day, continue up the Noirmont ridge.
new.q: Lac des Rousses, Les Rousses

new.title: Taste Comté at the Maison du Comté in Poligny
new.desc: The visit is a self-guided tour of Comté production, ending with a tasting of Comté in a glass-walled room over a wooded park. The house reopened after renovation and is run by the Comté interprofession.
new.tip: Prices cited run from about 7 to 8.90 euros. Book workshops early.
new.q: Maison du Comté, Poligny

new.title: Cruise or paddle on Lac de Vouglans from Bellecin
new.desc: Bellecin is a lakeside base on the Vouglans reservoir with a beach and nautical centre. The tourist board lists commented cruises aboard the Louisiane and electric boats without a licence.
new.tip: Check dates and prices with the Jura Sud tourist office or the Bellecin base.
new.q: Base de Bellecin, Lac de Vouglans, Orgelet

new.title: Climb the Ballon de Servance, Haute-Saône's high point
new.desc: At about 1,216 m it is the highest point of Haute-Saône, inside the Ballons comtois nature reserve. Fort Scherer, built 1877 to 1879, crowns the summit, and the chaumes give views to the other Vosges ballons.
new.tip: A short loop starts at the Col du Ballon de Servance (1,157 m). Snowshoes in winter.
new.q: Ballon de Servance, Servance

new.title: Hike the Plateau des Mille Étangs from Belfahy
new.desc: Belfahy is the highest village in Haute-Saône and the GR 59 crosses the commune. The plateau's ponds and peat bogs were shaped by ancient glaciers, with a marked 7.9 km Tour de Belfahy.
new.tip: Follow the blue-ring waymarks. Some forest tracks are disrupted by tree felling.
new.q: Entrée du village, D98, Belfahy

new.title: Visit the Comté dairy at La Fruitière de Frasne
new.desc: This Haut-Doubs cooperative offers a commented tour of the workshop and ageing cellars with a tasting. Free dates were listed in summer 2026.
new.tip: Check dates and book with the dairy or Pontarlier tourist office.
new.q: Fruitière de Frasne, 2 rue de Bellevue, Frasne

new.title: Hike to the Belvédère de Gougnot above Ornans
new.desc: The viewpoint offers a 180-degree panorama over Ornans, the Vierge de la Roche du Mont and the Loue valley. A circuit via the Roche Bottine adds more viewpoints.
new.tip: Wear grippy shoes. The route is a few hours.
new.q: Parking départ Belvédère de Gougnot, Ornans

new.title: Soak in the thermal baths of Luxeuil-les-Bains
new.desc: The listed thermal establishment at 3 avenue des Thermes has been run by the Chaîne Thermale du Soleil since 1998. It offers cures and fitness treatments.
new.tip: Book treatments in advance and check current hours.
new.q: Thermes de Luxeuil-les-Bains, 3 Avenue des Thermes, Luxeuil-les-Bains

new.title: Join the Absinthiades festival in Pontarlier
new.desc: The annual festival is organised by the Friends of the Pontarlier Museum and celebrates absinthe and artists. The 2026 edition ran on 3 and 4 October with free museum access.
new.tip: Held in early October, so confirm next year's dates. The museum is at 2 place d'Arçon.
new.q: Musée de Pontarlier, 2 Place d'Arçon, Pontarlier

new.title: Taste Morteau sausage in the tuyé du Papy Gaby
new.desc: A smokehouse at Gilley near Morteau, the tallest tuyé in the Haut-Doubs at about 17 to 18 m. Visitors see Morteau and Montbéliard sausage and cured ham smoked in the drying room, then taste.
new.tip: Visits last about 30 to 60 minutes with sales on site. Confirm hours before going.
new.q: Le Tuyé du Papy Gaby, Cotey, Gilley

new.title: Sample absinthe at Distillerie Pierre Guy in Pontarlier
new.desc: A family distillery founded in 1890 by Armand Guy at 49 rue des Lavaux, still family-run. It stayed open during the absinthe ban by making other spirits, and shows its copper stills on a free 30-minute visit with tasting.
new.tip: Visits are free but timetables conflict across sources, so reserve on pontarlier-anis.com.
new.q: Distillerie Pierre Guy, 49 Rue des Lavaux, Pontarlier

new.title: Taste kirsch at Distillerie Paul Devoille in Fougerolles
new.desc: The family distillery was founded in 1859 and holds the EPV label. The guided visit follows the making of spirits and liqueurs and ends with a tasting, with a self-guided cellar of oak casks.
new.tip: Guided visits take about an hour, in sessions listed on the tourism sites. Free parking on site.
new.q: Distillerie Paul Devoille, 7 Rue des Moines Hauts, Fougerolles-Saint-Valbert

new.title: Taste vin jaune at Domaine Berthet-Bondet
new.desc: An organic family estate at 7 rue de la Tour in Château-Chalon, founded in 1985. Visitors tour 16th-century cellars and taste Château-Chalon and Côtes du Jura wines, including flor-aged whites.
new.tip: A cellar visit with tasting averages around 15 euros. Call 03 84 44 60 48 first.
new.q: Domaine Berthet-Bondet, 7 Rue de la Tour, Château-Chalon

new.title: Order poulet au vin jaune et morilles at Les Arcades in Arbois
new.desc: A restaurant at 20 Grande Rue where reviewers single out the generous Bresse chicken with morels and vin jaune.
new.tip: Listed as closed Mondays. Confirm that it is still operating before booking.
new.q: Les Arcades, 20 Grande Rue, Arbois

new.title: Taste four Jura wines at the Fruitière Vinicole d'Arbois
new.desc: A cooperative founded in 1906 after the phylloxera crisis, claiming to be France's oldest. A roughly 60-minute visit at 2 rue des Fossés shows the cellars and ends with a tasting of four wines.
new.tip: Book ahead for the tasting. Vin jaune is the one to try.
new.q: Fruitière Vinicole d'Arbois, 2 Rue des Fossés, Arbois

new.title: Eat trout with morels at Le Chavot in Ornans
new.desc: A restaurant at 24 rue Pierre Vernier with a terrace above the Loue. Diners praise the trout with morel mushrooms and the daily trout special.
new.tip: Ask for a terrace table in summer. Check opening days.
new.q: Restaurant Le Chavot, 24 Rue Pierre Vernier, Ornans

new.title: Share a Comté fondue at La Pinte Comtoise in Pontarlier
new.desc: A traditional Franche-Comté restaurant on rue Jeanne d'Arc whose menu includes Comté fondue and hot Mont d'Or in season. Gault&Millau lists a budget of about 34 euros per person excluding drinks.
new.tip: Book for evenings in winter. Mont d'Or is a seasonal speciality.
new.q: La Pinte Comtoise, Rue Jeanne d'Arc, Pontarlier

new.title: Eat Franc-Comtoise dishes at La Petite Fontaine in Gray
new.desc: A traditional bistro at 17 bis quai Mavia with a direct view of the Saône and the river port. It serves Franche-Comté cooking and has a terrace on the water.
new.tip: A budget of roughly 15 to 28 euros is quoted. Check the hours.
new.q: La Petite Fontaine, 17 bis Quai Mavia, Gray

new.title: Try croûte au vin jaune at Le Bistrot des Marronniers
new.desc: A traditional bistro at 22 rue de Vallière in Lons-le-Saunier. The menu lists egg cocotte with Comté and Macvin sauce and mushroom croûte with vin jaune cream.
new.tip: The market menu was quoted at 37.95 euros, so check the current price.
new.q: Le Bistrot des Marronniers, 22 Rue de Vallière, Lons-le-Saunier

new.title: Eat Montbéliard sausage at La Pause Gourmande
new.desc: A restaurant at 4 bis rue du Château in Montbéliard whose terroir menu changes every four months. Its Franc-Comtoise plate pairs Montbéliard sausage with bone-in ham and cheeses.
new.tip: Best for lunch in the old town. Check opening days.
new.q: La Pause Gourmande, 4 bis Rue du Château, Montbéliard

new.title: Buy Morbier and Comté at the Fruitière de Morbier
new.desc: The Fruitière de Grande Rivière in Morbier makes Morbier and Comté and has a visitor gallery and shop. A Sentier du Morbier combines it with an organic cattle farm in Morbier.
new.tip: The shop sells Comté, Morbier, butter and cream. Check visiting hours.
new.q: Fruitière de Grande Rivière, 12 Hameau Les Chauvins, Grande-Rivière Château

new.title: Eat river sandre at La Plage in Gray
new.desc: A riverside restaurant on the Saône specialising in river fish, notably sandre, with a large terrace. A budget of roughly 15 to 30 euros is quoted.
new.tip: Best in summer for the terrace. Confirm opening hours.
new.q: La Plage, Route de la Plage, Gray
